aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/cover.title: Cover
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/cover.description: Gives -Dice on ranged attacks regardless of distance. Usually provided by terrain and/or map objects, as well as other creatures.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/heroi.title: Heroic Bleedout
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/heroi.description:
State activated when Vitals drop below 0. In this state you lose 2 AP Regen for every 1 Vitals below 0. Should your Stored AP reach 0 (either by being taken away through negative Regen, or by one last action), your character Dies.
Alternative: Damsely Faint - when reduced below 0 Vitals you may instead choose to Faint, thus be removed from the Combat and hope your companions can finish the fight without you. Less risk of losing your character, but less agency in what happens next. Great for a bathroom break.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/hit-p.title: Hit Points
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/hit-p.description: This is what AER Monster Rules use when referring to the enemy's Vitals. Reduces confusion between parts relating to Player and Foe, but they are more or less equivalent.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/immun.title: Immunity
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/immun.description: Reduces incoming DMG of a given type to 0. Cannot be influenced further.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/react.title: Reaction
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/react.description: Spending AP, or in the case of AER Monster Rules Dominance Points to act outside one's Turn, usually during another creature's action and on being provided a Trigger of sorts.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/resis.title: Resistance
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/resis.description: Reduces incoming DMG of a given type by 1, to no set minimum. With enough Resistance you may regenerate Vitals, or HP from certain attacks or Skills.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/round.title: Round
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/round.description: The amount of time it takes every creature in Combat to take their Turn. It is usually assumed 6 AP (or 3 AC) worth of Actions takes around 3 seconds, but this conversion is not often useful.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/spam-.title: Spam Penalty
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/spam-.description: The second activation of the same Skill Instance in a single turn costs +2 AP per activation. Does not apply to weapon Attacks.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/turn..title: Turn
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/combat/turn..description: Part of a Round. AER Monster Rules take theirs in a set order, while Players may intervene between those, either one at a time, or all together. Regardless, unless specified otherwise, each creature can only take One Turn per Round.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/damage-types.description: Ice: Deals Physical damage and applies a stack of Brittle. The next Skill or Attack made against a Brittle enemy gets +Dice.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/damage-types.title: Psychic
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/damage-types.description: Psychic: Applies -Dice to the target's next action corresponding to any damage amount greater than 1 (e.g., 2 damage becomes 1 damage and 1x -Dice). A single damage point will not apply -Dice, instead dealing damage as normal.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/resources/sp.title: Speed

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/-dice.html.title: -Dice
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/-dice.html.description: Modify Resolution. Stackable. For every stack roll an extra die, then pick the lowest value rolled among the results.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/+dice.html.title: +Dice
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/+dice.html.description: Modify Resolution. Stackable. For every stack roll an extra die, then pick the highest value rolled among the results.

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/aether-sickn.title: Aether Sickness
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/aether-sickn.description:
Aether represents perfect reality and the balance of nature. Over-absorption overwhelms the soul.
Characters can only benefit from Aether-Magic healing up to half their Max HP per Sanctuary Rest.
Beyond the Cap: Roll a d12 whenever you are healed by Aether.
First instance beyond the cap: Sickness only on a roll of 1.
Each subsequent instance: Increase the failure range by your Max HP. (e.g., a character with 5 Max HP fails on a 1-6 on their second healing instance beyond the cap).
Effects: When subject to Aether Sickness, you enter a catatonic state, inversing the Heroic Bleedout
state - Losing 2x AP per HP over 0. (A character with 3 HP, when sick, would lose 6 AP). The Sickness
passes after you’ve gone into negative AP, or HP, as you violently rid your system of the excess Aether

aer/core-rules-and-concepts/sanctuary-re.title: Sanctuary Rest
aer/core-rules-and-concepts/sanctuary-re.description:
Places safe from both environmental (weather, terrain) and creature-based threats. It should ideally have some form of enrichment or activity (a library, a forge, etc.). Resting here restores full HP and Armor Pips and grants milestone SP (extra SP from enriched locations).Sanctuary Checklist:
Friendly? (No Hostiles aware of you)
Comfortable? (Bedrolls, thick moss, pillows)
Secured? (Easily Defended, preferably guarded)
Insulated? (Safe from the weather and climate)
Sanctified? (Against Intrusions)
Provisioned? (Food, drink)
Unsafe Spots: Resting in an unsafe location (ones that don't meet 4/6 of the above requirements) carries risk (ambush, robbery, etc.). It only restores half of
your max HP and Armor Pips and does not grant SP. If you set up a guard duty, those on watch do not gain the benefits of the rest at all.

aer/enemy-blocks/aer-monster-rules.html.title: AER Monster Rules
aer/enemy-blocks/aer-monster-rules.html.description: The enemies should deal enough damage to be considered threats, and take enough damage to be satisfying to dispatch. The statblocks should be lightweight, clear, and easily skimmable for info.While players get AP for their turns, it would be too troublesome to track a 1-12 value for every enemy on the battle map. As such, for the convenience of the DM, the Action Clusters were developed, monsters get limited Action Clusters. Example Action Cluster Actions would be; 1 AC cost: Move 3 Spaces and make a single weapon attack, if possible. 2 AC cost: Make a ground slam AoE attack. 4 AC cost: Open a portal to the underworld, allowing imps to flood from therein.Dominance is an original system which helps outnumbered enemies shine a bit brighter than usual. The party’s AP Regen is added together, and is divided by the sum of Enemy AC enemies gain 1 Dominance Point at the start of their turn. These allow for a couple of general Dominance Actions, as well as monster-specific ones, giving them a bit of a “last stand” once the players get the upper hand. Sum of Playerside AP Regen / Sum of Enemy Action Clusters = Dominance Points at Round Start Types: meant to give an idea to the DM skimming through the monster manual about how “important” or “influential” an enemy may be. ♕ Centrepiece. 7 AC. 5 DP. ♖ Elite. 5 AC. 3 DP. ♙ Minion. 3 AC. 1 DP.Meant to give insight into how the monster behaves in combat. Most enemies have a combination of two Roles, order does not matter, but some may have the same role twice, highlighting their focus. ♥️ - Brawler. Frontline that's tough to break through. May have area attacks. ♣️ - Commander. Buffs allies, Debuffs enemies. May summon reinforcements. ♦️ - Duellist. Single target focus, high damage, glass cannon, or all three. ♠️ - Skirmisher. Either fully ranged, with ranged capability, or simply a very mobile enemy.Hit Points, Physical and Magical Armours – the general survivability of the monster. Each of these values contributes to the overall durability.

While humanoid from a distance, an up-close look reveals their skin to be made of carved stone, metal, or even ceramics. Their faces are smooth and featureless from the mouth up. They waged the First War and believe themselves superior to other races, especially the short-lived mortal ones. They are now mythic figures pursuing ancient agendas.... Psychic: You perceive the world through a blindsense, being able to sense things through Cover and in all directions, but only up to 30 Hexes.
You may Concentrate (2 Action Points) to narrow Your vision into a 60 Hex line.
